case_name: Manish Singh vs State Govt Of Nct And Ors.

parties.respondent_defendant: State Govt Of Nct And Ors., parents and others

facts_of_case: Petitioner Manish Singh seeks release of his wife Suman, allegedly detained by her parents against her wishes. They eloped and got married on 17th May, 2005 at Arya Samaj Mandir, Jamuna Bazar, Delhi.

legal_principles.principle: A person who is on the verge of majority, having reached the age of discretion, had accompanied someone of their own volition without any kind of enticement or inducement or force from anyone.
legal_principles.held: There was, thus, no taking away or enticing of a minor out of the keeping of a lawful guardian.
cited_cases: S. Varadarajan v. State of Madras, (1965) Supreme Court 942

legal_principles.principle: A girl who is between the age of 16 to 18 years had left her home and got married with a person of her choice, and she could not be made to stay in a remand home against her wishes.
legal_principles.held: The girls were steadfast in their resolve to live with their spouses.
cited_cases: Ravi Kumar v. The State and Anr., (2005) VIII AD (DELHI) 256
Shikha Sharma v. The State and Anr., (2005) VIII AD (DELHI) 256
Phoola Devi v. The State and Ors., (2005) VIII AD (DELHI) 256
use_in: habeas corpus petitions involving minor girls

outcome.final_order: Suman was permitted to accompany her parents.

keywords: Latin maxim: Actus me invito, nullum est
use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for habeas corpus
advising on marriage and co-habitation laws
assisting in cases of alleged abduction
